newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB head says Australia economy pace slow.
newsitem.headline: NAB head says Australia economy pace slow.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Thursday that the Australian economy was starting to move in a positive direction but not at a fast enough pace.
"It's probably not moving as quickly yet as we'd like to see,"Argus told reporters.

Referring to NAB's latest quarterly business survey released earlier on Thursday, which shows the economy being relatively flat, Argus said the economy was still not showing a level of confidence the government has been hoping would emerge.

Asked if Australia was overdue for a rate cut to further stimulate the economy, Argus said: "If you're not getting the benefits out of the last rate cut coming through into the economy, then yes, there is room for another rate cut."

Commenting on recent criticism by the Australian government that local banks were failing to pass on the full benefits of rate cuts to customers, Argus said Australian banks needed to "sit down with the government and probably educate them about the formation of financial services balance sheets."
Australian business conditions remained relatively subdued in the June quarter, consistent with underlying growth of 2.5 to three percent, the NAB survey found.
In aggregate terms, trading conditions improved slightly during the second quarter of 1997, but profitability performance deteriorated a little further and there was continued job shedding, it said.
National Australia Bank is Australia's largest bank.
